items: Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Conditions: Branching a program with if, elseif, else and match.
Data Mapper: A layer that moves objects to and from storage without the object knowing SQL.
Factory Pattern: Creating objects through a dedicated creator instead of new at every call site.
Interfaces: A pure contract of method signatures with no implementation.
Persistence Patterns: Patterns that map objects to storage: data mapper, identity map, unit of work.
Type-Checking Functions: is_*, gettype and friends that inspect a value type at runtime.

8596.title: Here is an implementation of a base class for update factories
8596.code:
<?php
abstract class UpdateFactory
{
    abstract public function newUpdate(DomainObject $obj): array;

    protected function buildStatement(string $table, array $fields, ?array

    $conditions = null): array
    {
        $terms = array();

        if (! is_null($conditions)) {
            $query = "UPDATE {$table} SET ";
            $query .= implode(" = ?,", array_keys($fields)) . " = ?";
            $terms = array_values($fields);
            $cond = [];
            $query .= " WHERE ";

            foreach ($conditions as $key => $val) {
                $cond[] = "$key = ?";
                $terms[] = $val;
            }

            $query .= implode(" AND ", $cond);
        } else {
            $qs = [];
            $query = "INSERT  INTO {$table} (";
            $query .= implode(",", array_keys($fields));
            $query .= ") VALUES (";

            foreach ($fields as $name => $value) {
                $terms[] = $value;
                $qs[] = '?';
            }
            $query .= implode(",", $qs);
            $query .= ")";
        }

        return [$query, $terms];
    }
}

8597.title: Here’s a concrete UpdateFactory class
8597.code:
<?php
class VenueUpdateFactory extends UpdateFactory
{
    public function newUpdate(DomainObject $obj): array
    {
        // note type checking removed
        $id = $obj->getId();
        $cond = null;
        $values['name'] = $obj->getName();

        if ($id > 0) {
            $cond['id'] = $id;
        }

        return $this->buildStatement("venue", $values, $cond);
    }
}

8599.title: Here is the base class
8599.code:
<?php
abstract class SelectionFactory
{
    abstract public function newSelection(IdentityObject $obj): array;

    public function buildWhere(IdentityObject $obj): array
    {
        if ($obj->isVoid()) {
            return ["", []];
        }

        $compstrings = [];
        $values = [];

        foreach ($obj->getComps() as $comp) {
            $compstrings[] = "{$comp['name']} {$comp['operator']} ?";
            $values[] = $comp['value'];
        }

        $where = "WHERE " . implode(" AND ", $compstrings);

        return [$where, $values];
    }
}

8600.title: Here is a concrete SelectionFactory class
8600.code:
<?php
class VenueSelectionFactory extends SelectionFactory
{
    public function newSelection(IdentityObject $obj): array
    {
        $fields = implode(',', $obj->getObjectFields());
        $core = "SELECT $fields FROM venue";
        list($where, $values) = $this->buildWhere($obj);

        return [$core . " " . $where, $values];
    }
}
8600.explanation: Once again, this class defines the public interface in the form of an abstract class. newSelection() expects an IdentityObject. Also requiring an IdentityObject, but local to the type, is the utility method, buildWhere(). This uses the IdentityObject::getComps() method to acquire the information necessary to build a WHERE clause, as well as to construct a list of values, both of which it returns in a two-element array.
